ORAL ORDER (PER : HONOURABLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE MRS. JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL)
1.

The petitioner herein is claiming a writ in the nature of certiorari seeking for quashing of the award dated 07.12.2011 with respect to Survey No. 310 paiki (old) Survey No. 1067, admeasuring Patel Mukeshbhai Prahladbhai vs State Of Gujarat on 11 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/6627937/
1 3685 sq. Mtrs. situated at village Kanj, Taluka Detroj, District Ahmedabad, which were acquired for the construction of Viramgam -2 Branch Canal, Bhimgadh Distributory Gatisana Minor Canal and further seeks a Writ of Mandamus commanding the respondents to NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined initiate fresh proceedings for acquisition of the land-in- question and for demand of compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabiliation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
2. To press his claim in the instant petition, it is stated that the petitioner had purchased the land-in-question vide registered sale deed dated 31.05.2006, entry of which was made in the revenue records on 06.08.2010 in favour of the petitioner.

entities.text: to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabiliation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The said entry was certified and a pakka entry was made on 02.11.2010.
In the meantime, the land-in- question was acquired by notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 dated 22.11.2010.

On conclusion of the acquisition proceedings, the consent award dated 07.12.2011 had been passed and compensation has been paid to the original owner namely respondent No. 2.
3.

It is sought to be submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that in view of the mutation of the name of the petitioner in the revenue records namely Form No. 6 on NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined 06.08.2010
, the respondent authorities had committed an error of law in entering into the consent award with the original owner and making payment of compensation to him.
4. On the said statement made in the writ petition, we require the respondents to file affidavit of the Collector bringing on record the proceedings undertaken by the respondents.

From perusal of the affidavit of the Collector, in the order dated 06.12.2023, it was recorded that there was no disclosure about the notice having been issued in accordance with Section 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894,
in the affidavit of the Collector, though there is a reference of Section 4 and 6 notification therein.
It was directed that the Collector shall file additional affidavit to bring on record the statement with regard to publication of notice under Section 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
In the additional affidavit filed on behalf of Collector, it is stated that the Panch Rojkam had been carried out under Section 9 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 on 24.11.2011.

A copy of the Panch Rojkam is appended at Annexure R-1 to the said NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED:
11/01/2024 undefined affidavit and it is stated therein that hearing had been conducted in accordance with Section 9 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, wherein the respondent No. 4, the original owner remained present and had submitted that the land-in- question was irrigated by means of bore-well owned by himself.

5. Taking note of the above statement in the affidavit of the Collector, we may go through the provisions of Section 9 of Land Acquisition Act, 1894, which reads as under : -
"9. Notice to persons interested.

- (1) The Collector shall then cause public notice to be given at convenient places on or near the land to be taken, stating that the Government intends to take possession of the land, and that claims to compensations for all interests in such land may be made to him.

2

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (2) Such notice shall state the particulars of the land so needed, and shall require all persons interested in the land to appear personally or by agent before the Collector at a time and place therein mentioned (such time not being earlier than fifteen days after the date of publication of the notice), and to state the nature of their respective interests in the land and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests, and their objections (if any) to the measurements made under section 8.
The Collector may in any case require such statement to be made in writing and signed by the party or his agent.

(3) The Collector shall also serve notice to the same effect on the occupier (if any) of such land and on all such persons known or believed to be interested therein, or to entitled to act for persons so interested, as reside or have agents NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined authorized to receive service on their behalf, within the revenue district in which the land is situate.

(4) In case any person so interested resides elsewhere, and has no such agent, the notice shall be sent to him by post in letter addressed to him at his last known residence, address or place or business and [registered under sections 28 and 29 of the Indian Post Office Act, 1898 (6 of 1898)]."
6. A bare reading of the said provision indicates that prior to taking of the possession of the acquired land, the Collector is required to cause a public notice at a convenient places on or near the land to be taken, stating the intention of the Government to take possession of the land and further that claims to compensation for all interests in such land may be made to him.

Sub-section (2) of Section 9 provides that notice shall state the particulars of the land so needed, and shall require all persons interested in the land to appear personally or by agent before the Collector at a time and place therein mentioned, and to state the nature of their respective interests in the land and the amount and particulars of their claims to compensation for such interests, including their objections, if any,
to the measurements made under section 8.
The Collector is mandated to require such statement to be made in writing NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined and signed by the party or his agent.

7. In light of the above provision, if the contention of the petitioner herein is accepted that he had purchased the land-in-question by virtue of the sale deed dated 31.05.2006 and entry of his name was made in the revenue records on 06.08.2010, we fail to understand as to why the petitioner would not participate in the land acquisition proceedings and would not submit his claim of being person interested in the land-in-question.
8. The notification under Section 4 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 was issued on 22.11.2010, and Section 6 notification was issued on 28.03.2011.
Section 9 notice had been published as per the Rojkam dated 24.11.2011 prior to the declaration of the award dated 07.12.2011.

3 9.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no averments in the writ petition which has been filed after about a period of more than 11 years to state as to whether the petitioner has ever participated in any of NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined the proceedings before the Collector during the course of acquisition of the land-in-question.
Section 9 is the public notice giving particulars of the land-in-question inviting all persons interested in the land to lay their claim for compensation or raise objections, if any.

At that stage, the petitioner did not participate rather the claim was put up by the original owner whose name was recorded in the revenue record at the time of preparation of land acquisition proposal.
In any case, there was no occasion for the land acquisition authorities to know about the right of the petitioner in the land-in-question.
10. In the said situation, for own inaction of the petitioner, he cannot claim for quashing of the award dated 07.12.2011 which is a consent award passed with the consent of the original owner.

The prayer made in the writ petition for initiation of the fresh proceedings of acquisition of the land-in-question and payment of the compensation under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabiliation and Resettlement Act, 2013, NEUTRAL CITATION C/SCA/17346/2023 ORDER DATED: 11/01/2024 undefined is misconceived.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabiliation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 11. For the aforesaid, the writ petition stands dismissed.
Liberty is with the petitioner to agitate his claim against the original owner, who was the vendor of the sale deed executed in his favour.
Pending Civil Application/s, if any, shall also stand disposed of.
